test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 27 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following rulers mobilise a large standing army in Delhi due to the Mongol invasion, which posed a huge administrative challenge?

I. Alauddin Khalji

II. Muhammad Tughluq
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Alauddin Khalji** mobilized a large standing army in Delhi as a response to the **Mongol invasions**, which posed a serious threat to the Sultanate during his reign. He strengthened the military infrastructure by building forts and increasing the size of the army. *Hence, statement I is correct.* 
• **Muhammad bin Tughluq** also faced challenges from Mongol invasions and organized a large standing army. He introduced reforms in administration and taxation to support the military expenses. *Hence, statement II is correct.* 
• **Mongol invasions** were frequent during the Delhi Sultanate period, and both rulers had to adapt their strategies to defend their territories effectively. 
• The mobilization of a large army posed **administrative challenges**, including logistics, financing, and coordination, which both rulers had to address through various reforms. 
• **Both I and II** are correct as both Alauddin Khalji and Muhammad bin Tughluq played significant roles in countering the Mongol threat through military and administrative measures. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Mongol Invasions:** 
• The **Mongol Empire** was one of the largest empires in history, originating from Central Asia under the leadership of **Genghis Khan**. 
• During the Delhi Sultanate period, Mongol invasions were frequent, targeting northern India, especially the regions around Delhi. 
• These invasions caused widespread destruction and posed a significant threat to the stability of the Sultanate. 
• **Alauddin Khalji's Military Reforms:** 
• Alauddin Khalji established a large standing army to counter the Mongol threat and maintain the security of his empire. 
• He introduced strict measures to ensure the efficiency of his army, such as regulating the prices of goods to manage the expenses of soldiers. 
• Forts were constructed, and he undertook extensive military campaigns to expand his empire and secure its borders. 
• **Muhammad bin Tughluq's Initiatives:** 
• Muhammad bin Tughluq faced Mongol invasions and organized a large army, but his methods often led to administrative difficulties. 
• He introduced innovative measures, such as token currency, to fund military operations, though these were not always successful. 
• His reign was marked by ambitious projects, such as shifting the capital to **Daulatabad**, which created logistical challenges. 
• **Impact on Administration:** 
• The mobilization of large armies required substantial resources, leading to reforms in taxation and administration. 
• Both rulers faced challenges in maintaining the morale and efficiency of their troops, as well as managing the logistics of warfare. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Key Challenges:** 
• The Mongol invasions highlighted the vulnerability of the Delhi Sultanate and necessitated robust military strategies. 
• Both Alauddin Khalji and Muhammad bin Tughluq demonstrated their ability to adapt to the changing geopolitical landscape through reforms and military actions. 
• **Historical Context:** 
• The Delhi Sultanate period was marked by frequent foreign invasions, requiring rulers to focus on military strength and administrative efficiency. 
• Both rulers are remembered for their contributions to the defense and administration of the Sultanate, despite facing numerous challenges. </ul
